faq.a: Abdelmajid represents Arabic عبد المجيد, meaning servant of al-Majīd (“the Glorious/Noble”).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdelmajid?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and المجيد.
Yes. The underlying compound is عبد المجيد (ʿAbd al-Majīd).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdelmajid?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; المجيد is related to م ج د, associated with glory and nobility.
Abdelmajid is a traditional Muslim name because it contains a compound invoking al-Majīd, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdelmajid as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdelmajid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of al-Majīd; the compound combines عبد with المجيد.
The supplied “ab-del-ma-jid” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abdelmajid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Abdelmajid as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
